links.outcome: Blinded board-certified oncologist ratings of real patient AI-generated plans and structure sets as good/acceptable/unacceptable
links.effect: Clinically acceptable results in 86% of fully automated cases vs 95% conventional; automated plans rated 'good' less often (12/22 vs 17/22), mainly due to smaller target delineation.
links.quote: Clinically acceptable results were achieved in 86% of fully automated cases compared with 95% in the conventional workflow.

links.outcome: Fully automated AI workflow compared with conventional clinical workflow on acceptability and processing time
links.effect: Acceptability 86% vs 95%; 'good' ratings 12/22 vs 17/22; median time 9 min vs 87 min; automated CTVs smaller (54.2 vs 68.3 cm3, p<0.001).
links.quote: The fully automated workflow required a median of 9 min (range 8-10) compared with 87 min (range 70-130) for the conventional workflow.

screen.reason: Prospective clinical comparison of a fully automated deep learning-based radiotherapy planning workflow versus conventional clinical workflow. Evaluates overall workflow accuracy and time savings, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard variation.
